title: Manager Guide: Hiring, Onboarding, Performance & Feedback (People Ops)
author: Ava Chen
body:
Purpose:
This guide gives managers a single, practical reference for Redwood Inference's hiring, onboarding, and performance processes. It summarizes required steps, templates, timelines, ownership, and links to detailed forms and systems. Use this as the primary checklist and source of truth when hiring, welcoming, and managing direct reports.

Scope:
Applies to all full-time employees, contractors with >6 month engagements, and managers responsible for hiring and performance processes across Redwood Inference. Recruiting operations and People Ops own system access and final approvals; hiring managers own role design, interviewing, onboarding experience, and performance conversations.

1) Hiring process overview
- Objective: hire high-impact candidates quickly while ensuring fairness, compliance, and strong candidate experience.
- Timeline target: 4–6 weeks from req approval to signed offer for most IC roles; 6–10 weeks for senior/lead roles that require final executive approvals.

1.1 Role and requisition
- Manager responsibilities: draft or update role profile (key responsibilities, success metrics, level, compensation band) and submit requisition in the HRIS (Greenhouse/Workday).
- People Ops: review banding, budget, and required approvals within 3 business days.

1.2 Interview loop & scorecards
- Use standardized scorecards aligned to role competencies (technical skills, problem solving, collaboration, ownership).
- Typical panel for IC roles: recruiter screen → hiring manager technical screen → cross-functional pairing/assignment → culture-fit / leadership interview → final manager interview.
- For senior roles add: hiring committee review and executive interview.
- Interviewers must complete scorecards within 48 hours of interview.

1.3 Offer and negotiation
- Hiring manager prepares offer summary (base, equity range, sign-on, start date, relocation/remote specifics) and shares with People Ops for final band confirmation.
- People Ops issues the offer letter and manages negotiation.
- Target offer acceptance: within 72 hours of initial offer.

1.4 Approvals & compliance
- All offers > band midpoint or with exceptional sign-ons require VP People Ops approval.
- For international hires, ensure right-to-work verification and local compliance checks before extending an offer.

1.5 Candidate experience & communication
- Provide candidates a clear timeline at first contact and update them proactively after each stage.
- Hiring managers should send a personalized note to finalists to strengthen engagement.

2) Onboarding: pre-boarding, Day 1, 30/60/90 and manager checklist
Intro: A structured onboarding improves retention and time-to-productivity. Managers are the primary driver of the new hire experience; People Ops provides templates, IT provisioning, and orientation sessions.

2.1 Pre-boarding (2 weeks before start recommended)
- Manager tasks (minimum): create first-week schedule, assign onboarding buddy, prepare 30/60/90 draft, request equipment, add to team calendar invites.
- People Ops tasks: HR paperwork, benefits enrollment window, orientation invites, accounts provisioning.

Pre-boarding checklist (table):
| Item | Owner | Target timing | Notes |
|---|---|---:|---|
| Signed offer & start confirmed | People Ops + Manager | Before start | Confirm tax/immigration docs if applicable |
| Equipment order (laptop, monitor) | Manager / IT | 7–10 days before | Use standard hardware spec unless approved otherwise |
| Account provisioning (Slack, GitHub, OKTA) | IT / People Ops | 3 days before | Raise access requests early for private repos |
| First-week schedule shared | Manager | 5 days before | Include orientation, team 1:1s, and training sessions |
| Buddy assigned | Manager | 5 days before | Buddy should be cross-functional when possible |

2.2 Day 1 (first day priorities)
- Welcome and team introduction (in-person or virtual).
- Manager 1:1 scheduled for 30–45 minutes to cover role expectations, immediate priorities, and social norms.
- Orientation: People Ops session on benefits, payroll, and company mission.
- Admin: ensure all accounts and physical access are functional; escalate any missing access immediately to IT.

2.3 30/60/90 framework (example milestones)
- 30 days: complete orientation, shipping first small task, meet cross-functional partners, confirm training plan.
- 60 days: take ownership of a larger deliverable, demonstrate core competency in primary tools, and participate in a team retro.
- 90 days: complete onboarding eval, meet initial success criteria, adjust goals for next quarter.

2.4 Manager checklist for first 90 days
- Weekly 1:1s (first month: twice weekly recommended for ICs in new domains).
- Clear objectives for month 1/2/3, with measurable success criteria.
- Introductions to key partners and teams.
- Provide regular feedback and document progress in performance system.
- Conduct 90-day onboarding review and share feedback with People Ops.

3) Performance & feedback cycles
- Redwood runs two formal performance touchpoints per year (Mid-Year and End-of-Year reviews) and supports ongoing check-ins and manager calibration cycles.
- Cadence: goal-setting at the start of each fiscal quarter, mid-quarter check-ins as needed, formal mid-year review (June) and annual review (December).

3.1 Goal setting and OKRs
- Managers should set 3–5 measurable objectives with each direct report for the cycle. Objectives should be specific, measurable, time-bound, and aligned to team/company priorities.
- Link goals to product milestones and SLOs where applicable.

3.2 Ongoing feedback and 1:1s
- 1:1 frequency: manager discretion, minimum every 2 weeks.
- Use the following structure for 1:1s: 1) updates on priorities, 2) blockers and support, 3) development/feedback, 4) action items.
- Encourage real-time praise and corrective feedback; document significant items in the HRIS.

3.3 Formal review workflow (mid-year / annual)
- Timeline: calibration → manager self-review → peer feedback → manager written review → calibration committee → final rating and calibration notes → compensation cycle (where applicable).
- Manager deliverables: submit draft review, collect peer feedback, schedule calibration panel discussion, and deliver a 1:1 performance conversation with the employee to walk through outcomes and development plan.
- Confidentiality: reviews and calibration notes are confidential; only share with HR and direct manager chain.

3.4 Performance improvement plans (PIP)
- Use PIPs for sustained performance gaps after coaching (not for single missed goals). PIP elements: specific expectations, measurable success criteria, timeline (typically 60–90 days), resources and support, and consequences if outcomes are not met.
- People Ops must be engaged before a PIP is initiated; legal may be involved for roles with contractual considerations.

4) Manager responsibilities and best practices
- Hire for mission and principle fit; involve cross-functional interviewers early.
- Onboard proactively: provide clarity, context, and early wins.
- Document feedback and decisions: keep notes in the HRIS and shared manager docs.
- Run regular 1:1s and set clear goals.
- Advocate for your team in calibration and compensation cycles.
- Escalate complex employee relations issues to People Ops early (within 48 hours of becoming aware).

5) Templates and examples (quick references)
- Interview scorecard example (short): role summary, rubric for competencies (1–5), hiring recommendation.
- 30/60/90 template: list measurable outcomes per month and mentors/owners.
- Offer summary template: base, equity %, sign-on, start date, relocation, manager name, approvals.
- 1:1 agenda template: status, block, feedback, development, action items.

6) Policies, compliance, and legal considerations
- Employment eligibility: verify ID and right-to-work documents before start date.
- Privacy: candidate and employee data must be stored in the HRIS only; do not share resumes or PII in public channels.
- Equal opportunity & anti-discrimination: follow Redwood's EEO policy; escalate any concerns to People Ops.
- Accommodation requests: managers must handle requests sensitively and route them to People Ops for reasonable accommodation planning.

7) Escalation and support pathways
- For hiring stalls: contact Talent Partner assigned to your req; if unresolved after 3 business days, escalate to Head of Recruiting.
- For onboarding tech/permissions issues: open a ticket in IT service desk and tag People Ops; target resolution within 2 business days.
- For performance or behavioral concerns: notify People Ops within 48 hours to align on next steps.

8) Ownership and metrics
- Manager: candidate selection, onboarding experience, performance coaching, and career conversations.
- People Ops: process governance, compliance, HRIS, and compensation recommendations.
- Recommended metrics to track: time-to-offer, offer-acceptance rate, new-hire ramp (time to first PR/feature), retention at 6/12 months, manager 1:1 frequency.

9) FAQ (common manager questions)
- Q: When should I use an external recruiter vs. internal hiring?
  A: If the role requires urgent bandwidth or niche skills not readily available in our pipeline, consult Talent Partner for external search.
- Q: How do I handle a late start/deferral request?
  A: Notify People Ops immediately; confirm offer terms and any changes to sign-on/relocation.

10) Resources and links
- People Ops handbook page: /confluence/company-handbook/people-ops-hiring-onboarding-and-manager-playbook-2026.json
- Interview scorecards & templates: shared drive link (People Ops/Templates)
- HRIS (Greenhouse/Workday) help: internal IT wiki page

Appendix: sample 30/60/90 (short)
- 30 days: complete onboarding checklist, meet 10 cross-functional partners, ship first small task.
- 60 days: lead a medium-scope project, own one CI/CD job or feature, present progress in team meeting.
- 90 days: demonstrate sustained delivery in primary area, propose goals for next quarter, receive final onboarding sign-off.

Document maintenance:
- Owner: People Ops (Ava Chen).
- Review cadence: annual review or after major policy changes.
- Change log: 2025-10-01 created; 2026-02-15 updated to include updated review cadence and PIP workflow.

Contact:
